910.name: Prehistoric and Early Settlement
910.description: The extraordinarily ancient human presence in Sri Lanka, the Balangoda Man remains, the Veddah aboriginal people, and the island's pre-Buddhist cultures in one of the world's oldest continuous human habitations.

sub_clusters.name: Balangoda Man and Prehistoric Cultures
sub_clusters.description: The Homo sapiens remains from Fa Hien Cave (one of the earliest outside Africa), the Balangoda Man skeletal remains, early stone-tool cultures, and the Veddah aboriginal people as descendants of the earliest settlers.
key_events: Fa Hien Cave yields evidence of Homo sapiens occupation dating to 125,000 years ago — among the earliest outside Africa

sub_clusters.name: Proto-Historic and Indo-Aryan Settlement
sub_clusters.description: The arrival of Indo-Aryan settlers from northern India, the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya from Bengal, and the development of early Sinhalese kingdoms.

910.name: Anuradhapura Kingdom
910.description: The ancient Anuradhapura kingdom — one of the longest-running continuous civilizations in history — the arrival of Buddhism via Ashoka's son Mahinda, the great stupas, and the hydraulic civilization's irrigation mastery.

sub_clusters.name: Buddhism's Arrival and Early Anuradhapura
sub_clusters.description: The founding of the kingdom, the mission of Mahinda and Sanghamitta bringing Buddhism and the sacred Bodhi Tree from India, the construction of the first great stupas, and the writing of the Pali Canon at Aluvihare.
key_events: Ashoka's son Mahinda introduces Theravada Buddhism to Sri Lanka (c. 250 BC)
The Pali Canon (Tipitaka) committed to writing at Aluvihare — the first time the Buddhist scriptures are written down (c. 29 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Great Stupas and Hydraulic Civilization
sub_clusters.description: The construction of the massive Ruwanwelisaya, Jetavanaramaya (one of the tallest ancient structures), and Abhayagiriya stupas, the development of the extraordinary tank (reservoir) irrigation system, and the Sigiriya rock fortress.
key_events: King Kashyapa I builds the Sigiriya rock fortress — one of the most dramatic sites in the ancient world (c. 477 AD)
Jetavanaramaya stupa completed at 122m — the tallest brick structure ever built (c. 300 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Chola Invasion and Fall of Anuradhapura
sub_clusters.description: The Tamil-Sinhalese tensions, the South Indian Pandya and Chola raids, Rajendra Chola I's devastating invasion that conquered Anuradhapura, and the shift of the capital southward.
key_events: Rajendra Chola I conquers Anuradhapura, ending over a millennium of the kingdom (1017)

920.name: Polonnaruwa Kingdom
920.description: The Polonnaruwa kingdom's liberation from Chola rule, the reign of Parakramabahu the Great, the magnificent ruins of the medieval capital, and the gradual decline under South Indian pressures.

sub_clusters.name: Vijayabahu's Liberation and Parakramabahu the Great
sub_clusters.description: King Vijayabahu I's liberation of Sri Lanka from Chola rule, the golden age of Parakramabahu I who unified the island and built the vast Parakrama Samudra reservoir, and the splendid architecture of Polonnaruwa.
key_events: Parakramabahu I unifies Sri Lanka and builds the Parakrama Samudra — the 'Sea of Parakrama' reservoir (1153–1186)
Parakramabahu I launches a punitive naval expedition against the Burmese kingdom of Ramanna (c. 1165)

sub_clusters.name: Polonnaruwa Decline and Drift Southward
sub_clusters.description: Magha of Kalinga's devastating invasion, the abandonment of Polonnaruwa, the shift of Sinhalese power southwestward through Dambadeniya and Yapahuwa, and the beginning of the Jaffna Kingdom.

920.name: Late Medieval Kingdoms
920.description: The Gampola and Kotte kingdoms, the independent Jaffna Tamil kingdom, the arrival of Arab traders, the spice trade, and the flourishing of Sinhalese Buddhist and Tamil Hindu culture before European contact.

sub_clusters.name: Kotte and Jaffna Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: The establishment of the Kotte kingdom near modern Colombo, the independent Jaffna Kingdom of the Tamil north, the thriving cinnamon and spice trade with Arab merchants, and the Sinhalese-Tamil coexistence.
key_events: Parakramabahu VI of Kotte briefly reunifies Sri Lanka for the last time under a Sinhalese king (1412–1467)

sub_clusters.name: Arab Trade and Muslim Communities
sub_clusters.description: Arab and Persian merchant settlement in Sri Lanka, the development of the Sri Lankan Moor community, the island's role in Indian Ocean trade networks, and the cinnamon, gemstone, and pearl trade.

930.name: Portuguese Colonial Period
930.description: The Portuguese arrival in Ceylon, the conquest of the coastal Kotte and Jaffna kingdoms, forced conversions to Catholicism, the cinnamon monopoly, and the heroic resistance of the Kandyan Kingdom.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Conquest and Kandyan Resistance
sub_clusters.description: The Portuguese capture of the coastal lowlands, the destruction of Buddhist temples, forced conversions, the Kotte royal family's conversion to Christianity, and the Kandyan Kingdom's fierce independence in the central highlands.
key_events: Portuguese arrive in Ceylon and gradually conquer the coastal kingdoms (1505–1597)
Kandyan Kingdom under Vimaladharmasuriya I defeats Portuguese attempts at highland conquest (1594)

930.name: Dutch Colonial Period
930.description: The Dutch East India Company's displacement of the Portuguese, the cinnamon trade monopoly, Roman-Dutch law, the development of canal systems, and the Kandyan Kingdom's continued independence.

sub_clusters.name: Dutch VOC Rule
sub_clusters.description: The Kandyan-Dutch alliance to expel the Portuguese, the Dutch monopoly on cinnamon, the introduction of Roman-Dutch law (still part of Sri Lanka's legal system), the canal building, and the British takeover.
key_events: Dutch expel the Portuguese and take control of Ceylon's coastal regions (1638–1658)
Roman-Dutch law introduced — elements persist in Sri Lanka's legal system to this day

930.name: British Colonial Ceylon
930.description: British conquest of Dutch Ceylon and the Kandyan Kingdom, the coffee and tea plantation economy, the introduction of Tamil plantation workers, constitutional reforms, and the path to independence.

sub_clusters.name: Conquest of Kandy and Plantation Economy
sub_clusters.description: The British conquest of the entire island including the fall of the ancient Kandyan Kingdom, the coffee blight and transition to tea, the import of South Indian Tamil labor for plantations, and colonial infrastructure.
key_events: Kandyan Convention — the last independent Sinhalese kingdom surrenders to the British, ending 2,300 years of indigenous rule (1815)
Coffee blight destroys the plantation economy; transition to tea makes Ceylon famous worldwide (1870s)

sub_clusters.name: Nationalist Movement and Independence
sub_clusters.description: The Buddhist revivalist movement, the Donoughmore and Soulbury constitutional reforms, universal suffrage in 1931 (first in Asia), and the peaceful transition to independence as the Dominion of Ceylon.
key_events: Ceylon becomes the first Asian colony to gain universal suffrage (1931)
Ceylon gains independence from Britain as a Dominion (4 February 1948)

940.name: Post-Independence and Rising Ethnic Tensions
940.description: Independent Ceylon's early promise, the Sinhala Only Act and Tamil marginalization, the republican transformation, the JVP insurrection, and the escalating ethnic tensions leading to civil war.

sub_clusters.name: Sinhala Only Act and Communal Politics
sub_clusters.description: S.W.R.D. Bandaranaike's Sinhala Only Act marginalizing Tamils, the 1958 anti-Tamil riots, the Bandaranaike-Chelvanayakam Pact's failure, Sirimavo Bandaranaike as the world's first female PM, and the 1971 JVP insurrection.
key_events: Sinhala Only Act makes Sinhala the sole official language, marginalizing Sri Lankan Tamils (1956)
Sirimavo Bandaranaike becomes the world's first female prime minister (1960)

sub_clusters.name: Republic and Rising Tamil Militancy
sub_clusters.description: The transformation from Ceylon to the Republic of Sri Lanka, the new constitution further centralizing Sinhalese-Buddhist dominance, the emergence of Tamil militant groups including the LTTE, and the burning of the Jaffna Library.
key_events: Ceylon becomes the Republic of Sri Lanka under a new constitution (1972)
Jaffna Public Library burned — 97,000 volumes destroyed, a deep wound for Sri Lankan Tamils (1981)

950.name: Sri Lankan Civil War
950.description: The devastating 26-year civil war between the Sri Lankan government and the LTTE (Tamil Tigers), the Indian intervention, suicide bombings, the tsunami, and the brutal final offensive.

sub_clusters.name: Black July and Early War
sub_clusters.description: The Black July anti-Tamil pogrom triggering full-scale civil war, the LTTE's rise under Prabhakaran, the Indian Peace Keeping Force debacle, and the IPKF's humiliating withdrawal.
key_events: Black July — anti-Tamil pogrom kills 3,000 and marks the start of the civil war (July 1983)
LTTE assassinates Indian PM Rajiv Gandhi with a suicide bomber in Tamil Nadu (May 1991)

sub_clusters.name: Eelam Wars and 2004 Tsunami
sub_clusters.description: The successive Eelam Wars, LTTE suicide bombings, the Norwegian-brokered ceasefire of 2002, the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami killing 35,000 in Sri Lanka, and the ceasefire collapse.
key_events: Indian Ocean tsunami kills approximately 35,000 in Sri Lanka (26 December 2004)

sub_clusters.name: Final Offensive and End of the War
sub_clusters.description: President Rajapaksa's decisive military campaign, the controversial final offensive against the LTTE in the Vanni, allegations of war crimes from both sides, and the killing of Prabhakaran ending the war.
key_events: Sri Lankan military defeats the LTTE; Prabhakaran killed, ending 26 years of civil war (May 2009)

960.name: Post-War Sri Lanka and Economic Crisis
960.description: The Rajapaksa dynasty's dominance, Chinese-funded infrastructure, the 2019 Easter bombings, the catastrophic 2022 economic collapse, the Aragalaya protest movement, and ongoing reconciliation challenges.

sub_clusters.name: Rajapaksa Era and Chinese Investment
sub_clusters.description: Mahinda Rajapaksa's post-war dominance, massive Chinese-funded infrastructure projects (Hambantota Port, Lotus Tower), accusations of war crimes accountability failures, Sirisena's surprise 2015 election victory, and the constitutional crisis of 2018.
key_events: Sri Lanka leases Hambantota Port to China for 99 years, raising 'debt trap' concerns (2017)

sub_clusters.name: Easter Bombings and Economic Collapse
sub_clusters.description: The 2019 Easter Sunday bombings killing 269, Gotabaya Rajapaksa's election, the catastrophic 2022 economic crisis (worst since independence), the Aragalaya protest movement storming the presidential palace, and Ranil Wickremesinghe's stabilization.
key_events: Easter Sunday bombings by ISIS-inspired terrorists kill 269 across churches and hotels (21 April 2019)
Sri Lanka declares sovereign default; protesters storm the Presidential Palace forcing Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee (2022)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
